name: Malta
snapshot: Robert Abela's Labour Party won a record fourth straight term in May 2026 in the EU's smallest member state, where rapid growth has strained housing and infrastructure.
culture: Maltese is the only Semitic language that is an official EU language, written in Latin script, reflecting Arab, Italian and British influences. The Knights of St John built Valletta, now UNESCO-listed. Village festas, with fireworks and processions for patron saints, fill summer weekends.
society: Malta's economy has boomed on online gaming, finance, tourism and, controversially, selling passports to rich foreigners, a scheme struck down by the EU's top court in 2025. Foreign workers now make up a quarter of the population. The 2017 murder of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia exposed corruption and links to politics.
situation: Robert Abela, prime minister since 2020, called an election for May 2026 and won a fourth consecutive term for Labour, a record. The Nationalist Party remains in opposition.
power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the majority in the House of Representatives, elected by single transferable vote in a near two-party system; the president is ceremonial.
